Kottamula Mallaiah And 2 Others vs The State Of Telangana And

The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Mummineni Sudheer Kumar
 Writ Petition No.2118 Of 2023
Order:

entities.text:
Kottamula Mallaiah And 2 Others vs The State Of Telangana And
4 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is the case of the petitioners that their father late Mr. Kottamula Gandaiah was originally assigned the land admeasuring Ac.1.20 gts. situated in Sy.No.512/149 of Eliminedu Viilage, Ibrahimpatnam Mandal, Ranga Reddy District, in the year 1968 and after his demise, the said extent of land was succeeded by the petitioners herein.
Petitioners herein also claim to have been in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the said extent of land.
2. While so, the respondents initiated land acquisition proceedings by issuing a notification No.G1/1162/2015, dated 28.03.2018.
However, neither the names of the petitioners herein nor their father's name was notified.
But, the acquisition proceedings were concluded without paying any compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners approached this Court by filing the present Writ Petition questioning the action of the respondents in not paying compensation for the subject land.

3. Respondent No.3 filed a counter affidavit admitting the fact of assignment of the subject land in the name of the deceased father of the petitioners and stating that after publication of declaration under Section 19(1) of the Right to Fair Compensation ::2::
MSK,J WP_2118_2023 and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act, 2013'), certain objections were raised for not publishing the names of the persons, who are in possession of the lands under acquisition and therefore, respondent No.5 conducted enjoyment survey and submitted the list through his Ref.No.B/536/2016, dated 22.02.2020.

The Mandal Surveyor of Ibrahimpatnam Mandal has submitted the sub-division record as verified from the enjoyment survey list and sub-division record of the Tahsildar stating that the names of the persons in possession as per the enjoyment survey have not been covered in the declaration and their names have to be included in the declaration under Section 19(1) of the Act, 2013 and certain persons/names who are covered by the declaration are not found in physical possession of the lands under acquisition as per the enjoyment survey and their names have to be removed from the declaration etc.

Basing upon the said survey report of the Mandal Surveyor, a revised declaration under Section 19(1) of the Act, 2013, was stated to have been published by duly withdrawing the previous declaration and accordingly, the compensation was paid to the persons in possession as per the enjoyment survey.

It is also stated that out of the total extent of Ac.1.20 gts. assigned in favour of the father of the petitioners,
petitioners are in possession only to an extent of Ac.0.20 gts.

sentences.text: and therefore, the petitioners are entitled for compensation only to an extent of Ac.0.20 gts., as the said extent of Ac.1.00 gts. was not occupied and cultivated.
It is further stated that, in spite of passing an Award for the said extent of Ac.0.20 gts.
in respect of which the petitioners are in physical possession, the petitioners have not come forward to receive the compensation and refused to receive the same.

Thus, it is further stated that some of the assignees have not occupied the land assigned to them nor cultivated the entire assigned land but have occupied and cultivated less extents and the balance vacant lands have been occupied by the villagers and being cultivated.
Thus, it is claimed that the compensation was paid to them as encroachers over the Government land to avoid any litigation in the matter.

Thus, it is stated that the petitioners are not entitled for compensation for the remaining extent of Ac.1.00 gts.
4.

From the above, it is evident that the father of the petitioners herein was admittedly assigned an extent of Ac.1.20 gts. situated in Sy.No.512/149 of Eliminedu Village and the same was succeeded by the petitioners herein.
The same was also recorded as such in the Revenue records.

But, when the said extent of land was sought to be acquired, the respondents, instead of following the provisions of law as contained in the Act, 2013, ::4::
MSK,J WP_2118_2023 appears to have adopted a strange procedure of resorting to conducting of an enjoyment survey on the alleged ground of certain objections raised by the persons in possession of the subject land.
The concept of conducting an enjoyment survey for the purpose of acquiring the lands under the provisions of the Act, 2013, does not find place in the said Act.

But, for the reasons best known, the respondents have adopted such an innovative procedure by empowering the Tahsildar or the Mandal Surveyor concerned to ascertain as to the physical possession and enjoyment of the land under acquisition and to pay the compensation basing upon such enjoyment survey.

5. Though, this Court specifically asked Sri Harender Pershad, learned Special Government Pleader,
to clarify the basis on which the said enjoyment survey was conducted and compensation was paid,
no such legal basis is brought to the notice of this Court that would authorize the respondents to conduct such enjoyment survey for the purpose of payment of compensation for the lands under acquisition.

In case, if there is any rival claim for payment of compensation or any objections were raised against the contents of the preliminary notification or the declaration made under Section 19 of the Act, 2013, or at the stage of an Award enquiry at the instance of so-called enjoyers, it is for the Land Acquisition Officer concerned to look into such objections and in ::5::
MSK,J WP_2118_2023 case, if there is any substance in such objection, the Land Acquisition Officer is supposed to proceed further to pass an Award and make a reference under Sections 76 and 77 of the Act, 2013, for adjudication of the rival claims for payment of compensation by the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority (for short 'LAR & R Authority').

But, in the instant case,
Kottamula Mallaiah And 2 Others vs The State Of Telangana And 4 Others on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175679085/
2 respondent No.3 had adopted a strange and innovative procedure without there being any legal basis and deprived the petitioners of the compensation for which they are otherwise entitled to.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For the reasons best known, no details of the so-called enjoyers to whom the compensation for an extent of Ac.1.00 gts. was paid are furnished in the counter affidavit nor any document in proof of payment of such compensation is also placed on record or to whom the compensation is payable
is not known and no such enjoyment survey report is also placed on record.

All this makes this Court to come to an irresistible conclusion that respondent No.3 has acted in a clandestine manner for extraneous considerations and deprived the petitioners of legitimate compensation for which they are otherwise entitled to under law.

As the payment of compensation on the ground of enjoyment survey is totally unknown to law and that is the only ground on which the petitioners are deprived of compensation for the said extent of land, this Court is of the considered view that ::6::
MSK,J WP_2118_2023 the petitioners are entitled for the relief sought for in the Writ Petition.
6.

Accordingly, the Writ Petition is allowed directing the respondents to pay the compensation by duly passing an Award/Supplementary Award in the name of the petitioners together with all the benefits, as may be entitled under the provisions of the Act, 2013, irrespective of payment of compensation, if any, paid to the so-called enjoyers, as expeditiously as possible, at any rate, within a period of three (03) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

In case, if the petitioners are not satisfied with the quantum of compensation arrived at by the respondents, it is open for the petitioners to take appropriate steps in accordance with law, after receipt of the compensation.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.
No costs.

MUMMINENI SUDHEER KUMAR, J Date:10.11.2023 NDS Kottamula Mallaiah And 2 Others vs The State Of Telangana And 4 Others on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175679085/
